 JUDGMENT

The petitioners have filed this Petition under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act seeking Compensation of Rs.25,00,000/- for the Death of one Mohammed Talha in a road traffic accident dated 23.06.2022.
2.

The case of the Petitioners' in brief is that:
On 23.06.2022 at about 11.00pm while the deceased was proceeding riding his scooter bearing Reg. No.KA-03-KG- 9257 on the flyover, near TIN factory Bus Stop,
Ring Road, SCCH-25 Bengaluru City, a Lorry bearing Reg.No.KA-51-B-2489 came with high speed, driven by its driver in a rash and negligent manner, so as to endanger human life and dashed against the Scooter.
Due to impact the deceased fell down and sustained severe injuries.
3. It is the further case of the petitioners that, immediately, he was shifted to nearest Bhagwan Mahaveer Jain Hospital for treatment.
Inspite of better treatment Sri.Mohammed Talha succumbed to the injuries.
The Post Mortem was conducted at Bowring and Lady Curzon Hospital, Bangalore.
Petitioners have performed funeral by spending Rs.50,000/-.

Prior to the date of accident, the deceased was hale and healthy, employed in a Garment Shop at Bangalore and earning Rs.20,000/-
per month.
The entire family was depending upon the earning of the deceased.

The accident was only due to the rash and negligent driving by the Driver of the said offending Lorry bearing Reg.
No.KA-51- B-2489.
The K R Puram Traffic police have registered a case and filed charge sheet against the driver of the said vehicle in SCCH-25 Cr.No.106/2022 p/u/Sec.279, 338 and 304A of IPC.
The respondents being the insurer and the insured of the said offending vehicle are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the Petitioners.
Hence, this petition.
4. In response to the service of notice, the Respondent No.1 appeared and filed written statement.
In spite of due service of summons, the respondent No.2 did not appear hence, placed exparte.
5. The objections of the Respondent No.1:
It has admitted the issuance of policy in respect of Respondent No.2 to the Tipper Lorry bearing Reg.No.KA-51- B-2489, it was in force as on the date of accident.

The police did not comply the terms and conditions u/Section 134 (c) and 158(6) of M.V.
Act.

The driver of the Tipper Lorry was not holding a valid and effective DL at the Kamal Basha vs Hdfc Ergo General Ins Co Ltd on 3 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/92357258/
2 time of accident.

sentences.text: It has denied the involvement of the Tipper Lorry in the accident.
Further the offending vehicle had no Permit and FC as on the date of alleged accident.
The deceased was dead due to self SCCH-25 accident from motorcycle bearing No.KA-03-KG-9257 which was being ridden under the influence of alcohol.
It has denied the age, income, avocation, medical expenses etc., and contended that the compensation claimed by the petitioners is highly excessive and exorbitant.

Hence,
prayed for dismissal of the petition.

6. On the above rival contentions of the parties, this court has framed the following issues:
1. Whether the Petitioners prove that, they are the legal representatives and dependents of the deceased Sri. Mohammed Talha?

2. Whether the Petitioners prove that, the deceased Sri.Mohammed Talha had died due to the injuries sustained in the Road Traffic Accident that occurred on 23.06.2022 at about 11.00pm on the flyover, near TIN Factory Bus Stop Ring Road,
Bengaluru, due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of Lorry bearing Reg.No.KA-51-B-2489 as alleged?
3. Whether the Petitioners are entitled for compensation? If so, how much and from whom payable 4.
What Order or Award?

On the other hand, the Respondent No.2 got examined its official Mr.Suresh G as RW.1 and got marked Ex.R.1.
8.
Heard both the Counsels and perused the materials on record.
The counsel for the petitioner has relied upon the following decisions.

(1)2023 Livelaw (SC) 531 : 2023 INSC 621, Mathew Alexander Vs. Mohammed Shafi & Anr.
(2) ILR 2015 Karnataka 1632, Krishnappa & Ors. Vs. Rarewala Engineering Works and Ors.

My finding to the above issues are as follows:-
Issue Nos.1 & 2: In the affirmative Issue No.3 : In the affirmative, Issue No.4 : As per final order for the Following:

REASONS 10. Issue No.1:
It is the case of the Petitioners that, the Petitioner No.1 is the Father, Petitioner No.2 is the Mother and Petitioner Nos.3 & 4 are the younger Sisters of the deceased - Mohammed Talha.
The Petitioners to prove their relationship have examined the 1st Petitioner as PW.1.
PW.1 has specifically spoken about this relationship in his chief- examination.
Apart from that, to prove the relationship, the Petitioners have also produced Notarized copy of Aadhar card of the petitioners as per Ex.P.10.
In Ex.P.15 - the Aadhar Card of the deceased, his father's name is mentioned as Mohammed Kamal Basha who is the petitioner No.1 in this case.
In the Aadhar Card of the Petitioner No.2, her husband's name is mentioned as Kamal Basha and in the Aadhar Cards of the Petitioner Nos.3 & 4 their father's name SCCH-25 is mentioned as Kamal Basha.
In Ex.P.4 - Inquest report of the deceased, his father's name is mentioned as Kamal Basha.
These documents are public documents and they have got initial presumptive value under law.
These documents have not been seriously disputed by the Respondents.
The Respondents have not produced any contrary documents to dispute and rebut the contents of documents produced by the Petitioners.
As such, there are no reasons to discard the oral and documentary evidence produced by the Petitioners.

Under such circumstances, relying upon the oral evidence of PW.1 and the documents, this court is of the opinion that the Petitioner No.1 is the Father, Petitioner No.2 is the Mother and Petitioner Nos.3 & 4 are the younger sisters of the deceased.
Accordingly, Issue No.1 is held in the affirmative.
11. Issue No.2:

The Petitioners to prove that the accident occurred due to the actionable negligence on the part of the driver of the offending Lorry have examined Petitioner No.1 as PW.1 and SCCH-25 produced documents as per Exs.P.1 to 8.
PW.1 has reiterated the averments of the petition in his affidavit filed in lieu of his chief examination.
During his cross examination he has admitted that the accident spot is a double Road with heavy traffic.
He has not challenged the charge sheet filed against his son.
On the other hand, the Respondent No.1 has denied the involvement and negligence of the insured vehicle.
It has examined its official as RW.1 and got marked Ex.R.1.

During the cross examination of RW.1 he has stated that the Lorry merged with the main Kamal Basha vs Hdfc Ergo General Ins Co Ltd on 3 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/92357258/
4 road from Benniganahalli cross road and was traveling in the left lane.

sentences.text: The charge sheet is filed against the deceased as well as the Lorry driver.

12. The documents produced by the Petitioners such as the FIR at Ex.P.1 in Cr.No.106/2022 of K.R.Puram Traffic Police with FIS, requisition to the Magistrate Court, PM report, inquest report,
sketch, spot mahazar, IMV report and charge sheet as per Exs.P.1 to 8 are all public documents and have initial presumptive value under law.

These documents fully and completely corroborate with the evidence of PW.1.
SCCH-25

The investigation officer in crime No.106/2022 of K R Puram Traffic Police has conducted the investigation in detail and has filed the charge sheet holding that the accident occurred due to the rash and negligent riding by the rider of the motorcycle bearing No.KA-03-KG-9257 and also on the negligent driving of the driver of the Lorry bearing No.KA-51- B-2489.
However, the Respondent No.1 has not obtained any contrary admission from the mouth of PW.1 to show the negligence of the deceased.

Therefore, there are no reasons to disbelieve the evidence of PW.1.
13.
The Inquest report produced as per Ex.P.4 and PM report produced as per Ex.P.3 clearly shows that 'Death is due to shock and hemorrhage as a result of multiple injuries sustained".

Ex.P.6 - MVA report shows that after testing of Two wheeler of the deceased bearing No.KA-032-KG-9257 has suffered damages to its front body shape on right side was scratched, front right side foot board and body scratched and rear right side safety grill was damaged and there was no SCCH-25 damages found on the offending Lorry bearing No.KA-51-B- 2489.
The counsel for the petitioner has relied upon the following decisions.
(i) 2023 Livelaw (SC) 531 : 2023 INSC 621, Mathew Alexander Vs. Mohammed Shafi & Anr.

(ii) ILR 2015 Karnataka 1632, Krishnappa & Ors. Vs. Rarewala Engineering Works and Ors.

sentences.text: Even though the respondent No.1 has contended that the deceased being under the influence of alcohol, none of the medical records show the same.
Therefore, this defence of the respondent No.1 is rejected.

On overall perusal of Exs.P.1 to P.7 and the charge sheet at Ex.P.8 it is clearly mentioned that the deceased was a rider in the two wheeler bearing Reg.No.KA-03-KG-9257 came with high speed, proceeding from Tin Factory towards Kasturi Nagar flyover applied sudden break and fell down on the road.
At that time a Lorry bearing Reg.No.KA-51-B-2489 came with high speed and ran over the deceased.
In spite of better treatment, the deceased succumbed to the injuries.

Therefore,
the chargesheet is filed against both deceased and driver of the offending Lorry.
However, the complaint is given by the father of the deceased which does not mention about the deceased applying brake and falling on the Road.
Only in the spot mahazar this fact is mentioned without any corroborating witnesses.

Therefore, on the evidence of PW.1 which has remained unimpeached during the cross examination and on SCCH-25 the basis of documents on record and relying on the decisions furnished above by the counsel for the petitioners, this Tribunal holds that the accident was caused due to the negligence of the offending Lorry Driver.
Accordingly, Issue No.2 is answered partly in the Affirmative.

15. Issue No. 3:
PW.1 has specifically spoken before this court that due to the untimely death of the deceased, they have lost the bread earner of their family and his loving son.
He has further deposed that he has spent more than Rs.50,000/- towards transportation of dead body and funeral expenses.
Therefore, the Petitioners are entitled for compensation as per the following discussion.
Monthly income 16.
According to the Petitioners, the deceased was employed at Garment Shop at Marathahalli and was earning a sum of Rs.20,000/- per month.
In this regard, the Petitioners have not produced any documents such as Bank statement, vouchers, etc., nor have they examined any SCCH-25 witness.
The accident occurred in the year 2022.
Under such circumstances, this court deems it fit to fix the notional income of the deceased at Rs.15,500/- per month for calculating the compensation.
Age of the deceased 17.
In so far as age of the deceased is concerned, the Petitioners have produced notarized copy of Aadhar Card as per Ex.P.10.
As per Ex.P.10 the deceased was aged about 25 years.
This is a public document and has got presumptive value under law.
This shows that as on the date of accident, the age of the deceased was 25 years.

(i) LOSS OF DEPENDENCY AND FUTURE PROSPECTS:-

sentences.text: As per the principles of law laid down in the case of Sarla Verma V/s Delhi Transport Corporation, appropriate multiplier applicable to his age is 18.

entities.text: Sarla Verma V/s Delhi Transport Corporation
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In the instant case, the deceased has a Father, Mother and two younger Sisters, aged about 55, 51, 26 and 18 years respectively.
PW.1 in his cross -examination stated that he has 5 children, elder son got SCCH-25 married.
His daughters have studied and do not work anywhere and are not married.
He is also not working any where.
As such it can be considered that petitioner Nos.1 to 4 are considered as the dependents of the deceased.

As such, the petitioners are entitled to get compensation.
18.
As per the decision of Hon'ble Supreme court in National Insurance company Vs Pranay Sethi and others(AIR 2017 S.C 5157) persons aged above 60 years are not entitled to any future prospects.

entities.text: National Insurance company Vs Pranay Sethi and others(AIR 2017 S.C 5157)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: As mentioned above, since the deceased was under 40 years age slab, 40% future prospects is to be added to his monthly income.
So Rs.6,200/- (Rs.15,500/- X 40% = Rs.6,200/-) should be added to his monthly salary of Rs.15,500/- then it comes to Rs.21,700/- per month.
As per the Sarala Verma case, if the deceased is a bachelor then 1/2 of his income has to be deducted towards his personal and living expenses.

However in case of Bachelor with large families being dependent on the deceased, 1/3rd has to be deducted towards personal expenses i.e., Rs.7,233/- has to deducted then balance SCCH-25 comes to Rs.14,467/- (Rs.21,700/- - Rs.7,233/-).
Therefore, the total loss of dependency would be Rs.31,24,872/- (Rs.14,467/- X 18 x 12) = Rs.31,24,872/-).

(ii) LOSS OF CONSORTIUM:-
In Magma General Insurance company Limited Vs. Nanuram (2018) 18 SCC 130

entities.text: Magma General Insurance company Limited Vs. Nanuram (2018) 18 SCC 130
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: , the Hon'ble Apex court has observed "Consortium" is a compendious term, which encompasses spousal consortium, parental consortium and filial consortium.
The right to consortium would include the company, care, help, comfort, guidance, solace and affection of the deceased, which is a loss to his family.
With respect to a spouse, it would include sexual relations with the deceased spouse".

19. This observation of the Hon'ble Supreme Court is reaffirmed in United Indian Insurance Company Ltd. Vs. Satinder Kaur @ Satvinder Kaur and others, (2021) 11 SCC 780.
SCCH-25 20.

entities.text: United Indian Insurance Company Ltd. Vs. Satinder Kaur @ Satvinder Kaur and others, (2021) 11 SCC 780
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The Petitioner No.1 is the Father and the petitioner No.2 is the Mother and the petitioner Nos.3 & 4 are the younger sisters of the deceased.
The Mother, father have to live remaining part of their life in the absence of their young son.
The loss of a young son full of hopes for the future can never be suitably compensated to the parents.
However, petitioner Nos.1 & 2 are entitled to a sum of Rs.44,000/- each (Total Rs.88,000/-) under the head of loss of consortium.

(iii) TRANSPORTATION AND FUNERAL EXPENSES AND LOSS OF ESTATE:-
Kamal Basha vs Hdfc Ergo General Ins Co Ltd on 3 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/92357258/
7

entities.text: Kamal Basha vs Hdfc Ergo General Ins Co Ltd on 3 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In so far as the funeral and transportation expenses are concerned, the Petitioners have contended that they have spent a sum of Rs.50,000/- towards transportation of dead body and funeral obsequies.
But, there is no document produced in this regard.
The deceased was at Bhagawan Mahaveer Jain Hospital for further treatment.
That inspite of treatment, he died during the treatment.
In addition there are expenses during the death of a person for which SCCH-25 documents cannot be maintained.

Therefore, in the interest of justice the Petitioners are awarded a sum of Rs.20,000/-
under this head.
If the deceased was alive he would have certainly saved some amount out of his living and personal expenses and created an estate in favour of the Petitioners.
Therefore, the Petitioners are entitled for Rs.20,000/- under the head of loss of estate.
(iv) MEDICAL EXPENSES:
PW.1 has contended that they have spent amount towards treatment.
In this regard they have produced 6 medical bills for a sum of Rs.1,24,638/-.
There is no contrary evidence to these bills from the Respondents.
Therefore, Petitioners are entitled to the above said amount under this head.
Therefore, the Petitioners are entitled for a total sum of Rs.33,77,510/-.

If it is rounded off it comes to Rs.33,77,600/-
SCCH-25 Liability 21.
The respondents have failed to prove the defences.
The respondent No.1 being the insurer has to indemnify the respondent No.2.
The petitioners have claimed compensation for a sum of Rs.25,00,000/-.

But the petitioners are entitled to a sum of Rs.33,77,600/- along with interest @
6% per annum.
Therefore, the petition needs to be allowed.
Accordingly I answer Issue No.3 in the affirmative.
22. Issue No.4:-

In view of the findings of the above issue Nos.1 to 3, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER
The Petition filed by the Petitioners under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act is hereby allowed with costs.

The Petitioners are entitled for Compensa- tion of Rs.33,77,600/- (Rupees Thirty Three Lakhs Seventy Seven Thousand Six Hundred only) along with interest at the rate of 6% p.a., SCCH-25 from the date of Petition till the date of deposit of the Award amount and interest.
The Respondent Nos.1 & 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the peti- tioners.

The respondent No.1 is liable to deposit compensation to the petitioners within 60 days from the Kamal Basha vs Hdfc Ergo General Ins Co Ltd on 3 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/92357258/
8 date of suit till its realization.
On deposit of the award amount and inter- est, Rs.8,00,000/- each shall be deposited in the names of the Petitioner Nos.2, 3 & 4 in any Bank of their choice for a period of 3 years and remaining amount shall be released to the petitioner No.1 by way of e-payment with proper identification and due acknowledgment.
The Advocate's fee is fixed at Rs.1000/-.
